summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted due to diarrhea and redness in her left arm one week after AV loop graft placement. Evaluation revealed cellulitis at the graft site and overflow diarrhea from opioid-induced constipation. She was treated with IV vancomycin, transitioned to oral doxycycline, and underwent two hemodialysis sessions. Her infection improved, white count normalized, and bowel symptoms resolved with a bowel regimen. Transplant surgery evaluated her for possible steal syndrome, recommending outpatient follow-up for potential graft ligation. She was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, avoid opioids, monitor graft site, and attend follow-up appointments.
